tagline: Know which tool to reach for — the Tenable MCP or navi.
lore: The Pointer freezes and aims its whole body at the quarry, so the hunter knows exactly where to go — here it points each job at the right tool: the Tenable MCP or navi.
problem: Teams with both the Tenable MCP and navi waste time on the wrong one — trying to tag 50,000 assets with a rule that caps out, or looking for an ACR writer that only one tool has — and lose trust when the two disagree.
does: The Pointer is a routing matrix: for each job — lookups, tagging small or at scale, OS / app / device tagging, ACR and AES, exports, SQL, scans, agents, policies, WAS, dashboards — which tool does it best, which can do it, and why. It lists the limits that force a hand-off and shows a navi-side snapshot to check what navi is pointed at.

glance.caption: MCP Compare's routing matrix: each job, whether navi and the Tenable MCP do it first-class (✅), possibly (☑) or not at all (—), and the reason.

capabilities: 15 common jobs, each routed to navi, the Tenable MCP, or either — with the reason.
rule-based tags cap at about 1,024 IPs / 1,999 UUIDs; OS, app and device tagging needs plugin-output fingerprinting; only navi writes ACR; native dashboards are Tenable-only.
suspect a stale navi.db first; different tenants are the rare case; navi can tell you which key and container it holds.
the tag categories, asset count and freshness navi sees right now.
how: The matrix and notes are reference content in the page; the snapshot reads your local navi.db. Nothing is written. The full "same account" check across both tools needs the Tenable MCP alongside navi.
who: Anyone using both the Tenable MCP and navi — engineers building workflows, and admins checking that both point at the same tenant.
better: Every tagging hound uses navi for the jobs the matrix routes there (tagging at scale, ACR, plugin-output detection); Anubis is the ACR writer it points to.
cta: Check the Pointer before you start — then use the right tool.
